identity.title: Understanding and Mitigating Numerical Sources of Nondeterminism in LLM Inference

problem.claim: The paper examines why LLM inference outputs and benchmark performance can vary across system configurations and numerical-precision settings.

gap.claim: The authors state that floating-point precision is often neglected in evaluation practices and that its effect on inference reproducibility lacked systematic investigation.

contributions.claim: A systematic investigation quantifying when and how hardware, software, batch-size, and precision choices cause LLM outputs to diverge.
An attribution of the variability to the non-associativity of limited-precision floating-point arithmetic.
LayerCast, a lightweight pipeline that stores weights in 16-bit precision while computing in FP32 to balance memory efficiency and numerical stability.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe this as the first systematic investigation of how numerical precision affects reproducibility in LLM inference.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that changing evaluation batch size, GPU count, or GPU version can produce significant response differences.

Under bfloat16 precision with greedy decoding, they report up to 9% accuracy variation and a 9,000-token response-length difference for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B across GPU and batch-size configurations.
The authors report that small early-token rounding differences can cascade into divergent reasoning chains and affect accuracy, especially in reasoning models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reliable benchmark interpretation depends on accurate and reproducible LLM performance.
System configuration changes can substantially alter generated responses, with especially large effects in reasoning models.
The authors trace the variability to non-associative floating-point arithmetic under limited precision.
Controlled experiments across hardware, software, and precision settings quantify output divergence and highlight neglected precision factors.
LayerCast retains 16-bit weight storage but uses FP32 computation for greater numerical stability.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a concrete configuration-sensitive result with a root-cause account involving early-token rounding and floating-point non-associativity.

lessons.interpretation: A claim becomes more actionable when its observed effect is connected to a plausible mechanism and the conditions producing it are retained.
lessons.application: When reporting reproducibility failures, state the affected metric, configuration conditions, magnitude, and proposed numerical mechanism together.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the mechanism is untested or when configuration details cannot be controlled or specified.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the full model, task, benchmark set, hardware matrix, or statistical methodology behind the reported variation.
No abstract-level evaluation results are given for LayerCast itself, so its practical stability or accuracy trade-offs remain unspecified.
The scope of the claimed first systematic investigation is not operationally defined.
